description: The overload NO contact form identifies a signal path associated with overload-device operation. Its destination may be a lamp, controller or alarm circuit and is separate from the contact used to interrupt the motor command.

This is a convention-specific lookup based on the publisher's IEEE-labelled preview. The geometry here is independently drawn to explain the connection or operation; it is not a certified reproduction of the standard graphic.
readingNotes: Verify the alarm contact state after reset.
Read the selected library and the project legend together. A vendor block identifier is meaningful within its named library and is not a universal standard-symbol code.
distinction: Overload alarm status and contactor closed-position status describe different equipment conditions.
